name: LM741CN_NOPB
title: LM741, LM741A, LM741C single general-purpose operational amplifier
summary: A single bipolar operational amplifier for general use, run from single or dual supplies up to ±22 V (LM741, LM741A) or ±18 V (LM741C). Its inputs and output are protected against overload, and it does not latch up when the input common-mode range is overrun. Two pins take an external trim for input offset. The LM741 and LM741A are specified from −55 °C to 125 °C, the LM741C from 0 °C to 70 °C; LM741CN/NOPB is the LM741C in an 8-pin PDIP.
key_figures: ±10 V to ±18 V (LM741C); ±10 V to ±22 V (LM741, LM741A); ±15 V nominal
2 mV typ, 6 mV max at 25 °C, RS ≤ 10 kΩ
200 V/mV typ, 20 V/mV min, RL ≥ 2 kΩ

notes: Three grades of one circuit: LM741, LM741A and LM741C. The LM741C figures hold over 0 °C to 70 °C where the LM741 and LM741A hold over −55 °C to 125 °C. The LM741A has tighter offset, bias and gain limits.

Packages: TO-99 metal can (LMC, 8 pins, 9.08 mm × 9.08 mm), ceramic DIP (NAB, 8 pins, 10.16 mm × 6.502 mm) and plastic DIP (P, 8 pins, 9.81 mm × 6.35 mm). The orderable parts are the LM741C in PDIP and as wafer sale.
The LM741H, in TO-99, is available to JM38510/10101. Military specifications are RETS741X for the LM741 and RETS741AX for the LM741A.
The PDIP marking is on two lines: LM over 741CN.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier, gain of 2
circuits.description: The signal goes straight into the non-inverting input, so the source sees the high input impedance of the amplifier and the output is in phase with it. R2 runs from the output back to the inverting input and R1 from the inverting input to ground; the gain is 1 + R2/R1, which is 2 with both at 4.7 kΩ. The amplifier runs from ±15 V. The offset null pins and pin 8 are left open.

parts.note: 5 % tolerance; feedback, output to inverting input

notes: Measured at ±15 V with a 10 kHz sine of 1 Vpp nominal from a function generator: 1.06 Vpp in, 1.94 Vpp out. The ideal gain is 2; including the 5 % resistor tolerance it is 1.992; the gain from the mean amplitudes on the oscilloscope is 1.83.
For a more accurate gain, R1 and R2 go to 1 % tolerance.
Each supply pin is decoupled with 0.1 µF placed as close to the pin as possible (C1 at V+, C2 at V- in the reference layout).

operation.text: LM741, LM741A and LM741C are one circuit. The LM741C is guaranteed only over 0 °C to 70 °C; the LM741 and LM741A over −55 °C to 125 °C. The LM741A carries tighter limits on offset voltage, offset current, bias current and gain, and adds drift and bandwidth figures.
In most uses the LM741 drops into a socket for the LM709C, LM201, MC1439 or LM748 with the same pinout, which lets it stand in for parts no longer made. It improves on the LM709.
It works from a dual supply or a single supply. Recommended supplies run from ±10 V to ±18 V for the LM741C and to ±22 V for the LM741 and LM741A, with ±15 V nominal.
Both the inputs and the output have protection against overload, and the output may be shorted for an unlimited time. Typical short-circuit current is 25 mA.
Driving the inputs past the common-mode range does not latch the amplifier, so it recovers without the supply being cycled. It is also free of oscillation.

Without feedback the open-loop gain is so high that a small difference between the inputs sends the output close to a supply rail, and the part acts as a comparator. With the inverting input at 0 V, a positive voltage on the non-inverting input gives a positive output and a negative one a negative output.
With part of the output fed back to the inverting input, gain falls, and the feedback network rather than the amplifier decides the circuit's gain and frequency response.

Pins 1 and 5 adjust the balance of the input stage to cancel input offset voltage. At 25 °C with ±20 V supplies the adjustment range is ±15 mV typical (LM741, LM741C) and at least ±10 mV (LM741A). Pin 8 has no connection and stays open.

The inputs are the bases of an NPN bipolar pair, Q1 (non-inverting) and Q2 (inverting). The offset null pins sit at the emitters of Q5 and Q6, each with 1 kΩ to the negative supply. Frequency compensation is an internal 30 pF capacitor, and the output transistors have 25 Ω and 50 Ω emitter resistors.
Comparators, multivibrators, DC amplifiers, summing amplifiers, integrators, differentiators and active filters.
Put 0.1 µF on each supply line, as near the LM741 supply pins as it will go.

For stability, watch the routing of leads, where parts sit and how the supplies are decoupled. A feedback resistor from the output belongs with its body next to the input it feeds; that keeps the input node's stray capacitance to ground small, which reduces pickup and pushes the feedback pole higher. In the reference layout both feedback resistors and both decoupling capacitors sit right against the DIP.
ESD protection on chip is limited. Store and handle the parts with their leads shorted together or pressed into conductive foam.
